sheet-80.description: Sheet 80 covers the centre of the Oceanic district of Rumson at 60 ft to an inch, a new sheet dated January 1922. Oceanic Road, marked as the main street, crosses the sheet near the top; below it four blocks run down between Allen, Lafayette, Washington and Bingham Avenue to Church Street at the bottom, and above it two blocks reach north to Hunt Street, with an open area marked Park west of Lafayette. The blocks are mostly residential, with frame dwellings, private garages and sheds on deep lots. Commercial and public buildings cluster along Oceanic Road: the Borough of Rumson Fire Department No. 2 with its siren tower at the Allen corner, the post office, a barber shop and an auto repair shop on the Lafayette block, and the Oceanic M.E. Church east of Lafayette. A boys' club stands on the Bingham block, and the public school, drawn in brick, fills the south end of the Allen to Lafayette block near Church Street. Water pipes of 6 and 18 inches run in the streets, with hydrants at most corners. House numbers are printed along every frontage. The margins name the adjoining sheets: 100 to the north, 99 to the east, 98 to the south and 79 to the west, the last belonging to another volume of the series. The sheet carries the title Rumson, Oceanic P.O., and a north arrow pointing to the upper right.
notes: Oceanic Road is today West River Road (East River Road east of Bingham Avenue).
Lafayette (Av.) and Washington (Av.) are today Lafayette Street and Washington Street.
Drawn at 60 ft to an inch, the largest scale in this atlas.
map, 60 ft to an inch (new sheet Jan. 1922). Oceanic district: Oceanic Rd (Main) = West River Road, Allen, Lafayette, Washington, Bingham Av, Hunt, Church. One part.

sheet-97-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 97, an additional sheet dated January 1922, is a small-scale sheet at 240 ft to an inch covering the western part of Rumson between the North Shrewsbury River and Ridge Road. Oceanic Road crosses the sheet below the river, continuing west as Fair Haven Road beyond Buena Vista Avenue at the west edge, which carries the note See Volume of Red Bank and Vicinity. North of the road, long riverfront lots run down to the water, with country houses, boat houses and garages of owners including J. G. Gillig, F. M. Smith, H. E. Meeker, H. S. Borden and B. H. Borden. South of the road the sheet is largely open estate land between Buena Vista Avenue and Bellevue Avenue, including the F. M. Smith place and Auldwood, the J. C. Hoagland estate, with its house, stables and outbuildings. At the east edge 3rd Street, William Street, Church Street, 2nd Street, 1st Street, Allen and Narumson Street outline the edge of the village blocks drawn in detail on sheets 79, 80 and 98. Ridge Road runs along the bottom. The lower right corner is occupied by an inset drawn separately (part 2). Water pipes along the roads are marked with their sizes.
notes: Oceanic Road is today West River Road; west of Buena Vista Avenue it is River Road in Fair Haven.
Margin note: See Volume of Red Bank and Vicinity.
At 240 ft to an inch the drawing is coarse; Ridge Road junctions sit 6 to 8 m from today's.

map, 240 ft to an inch. Part 1: west Rumson from Buena Vista Av to Allen, river to Ridge Rd (estates). Part 2: inset lower right, Borden farm between Narumson and Ridge Rd at Bingham Av, own border; two junctions only (helmert).

sheet-97-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 97 is an inset in the lower right corner of the sheet, framed by a heavy border and drawn at the same small scale of 240 ft to an inch. It shows the farm of H. S. and B. H. Borden between Narumson Street at the top and Ridge Road at the bottom, bounded on the east by Bingham Avenue. The ends of Allen Street, Lafayette Street and Washington Street are labelled where they meet Narumson along the top. Within the farm a group of buildings is drawn: a machinery house, corn crib, barns, a silo of 28 ft, a shed and a coop, with a dwelling near Bingham Avenue. A dimension line with the figure 1392 runs west from the buildings, and an arrow points towards sheet 98. The rest of the inset is open land. The margin numbers 98, 99 and 83 name the adjoining sheets.
notes: Narumson is today Narumsunk Street.
Placed from two junctions only (Bingham Avenue at Narumsunk Street and at Ridge Road): low confidence.

map, 240 ft to an inch. Part 1: west Rumson from Buena Vista Av to Allen, river to Ridge Rd (estates). Part 2: inset lower right, Borden farm between Narumson and Ridge Rd at Bingham Av, own border; two junctions only (helmert).

sheet-98.description: Sheet 98, an additional sheet dated January 1922 at 60 ft to an inch, continues sheet 80 southward in the Oceanic district of Rumson. It shows the long blocks between Church Street at the top and Narumson at the bottom, divided by Allen, Lafayette, Washington and Bingham Avenue, with a strip of lots west of Allen along the edge of sheet 97. The area is almost entirely residential: frame dwellings of one and two storeys with private garages, coops and sheds, on narrow deep lots lettered along each frontage. Red Men's Hall stands on Church Street east of Lafayette, and a dwelling with hollow tile walls is marked on the Washington block. A few storage buildings and a hall stand in the middle of the Lafayette to Washington block. Much of the southern half of each block is still open ground. Water pipes of 6 inches run along Allen, Lafayette and Church, with hydrants at intervals. The margins refer to sheet 80 to the north, 97 to the south and west, 79 to the northwest and 99 to the east. A north arrow at the upper right points to the upper right; the scale bar is printed in the lower margin.
notes: Narumson is today Narumsunk Street between Allen Street and Bingham Avenue.
Lafayette and Washington are today Lafayette Street and Washington Street.
map, 60 ft to an inch. Church to Narumson (= Narumsunk Street), Allen to Bingham Av. One part.

sheet-99.description: Sheet 99, an additional sheet dated January 1922 at 120 ft to an inch, covers the east side of the Oceanic district of Rumson. Along the west edge runs Bingham Avenue, and the large blank Parmly Property fills the western half. Oceanic Road enters at the top left, runs southeast to Forest and then turns south down the middle of the sheet towards Black Point Road. North of the road, long narrow lots run down to the North Shrewsbury River, which forms the northeast edge of the sheet; a creek divides them from a group of lots around Wilson Place. Between Forest and Oceanic Road a wedge of lots surrounds a small lake, south of which Lakeside Avenue crosses. Further south, blocks between Forest and Oceanic Road are cut by North and West streets, with the Summer Branch of the Babies Hospital of New York City in a large lot. East of Oceanic Road, Sanford Place, Parmly and Black Point Road cross Roosevelt (Centre) towards Avenue of Two Rivers on the east edge. These blocks hold dwellings, garages, several stucco and hollow tile houses and a Public Service sub-station. The margins refer to sheets 80 and 98 to the west, 100 to the north and east, 97, 83 and 81 to the south. A north arrow at the left points to the upper right.
notes: Oceanic Road is today East River Road.
Forest is today Forrest Avenue.
Sanford Place appears to be today's Ward Lane; Roosevelt (Centre) is Center Street; Parmly is Parmly Street.
Wilson Place is today Wilson Circle; its junction was left out of the fit because the drawn road layout there differs from today's.

map, 120 ft to an inch. Oceanic Rd (= East River Road), Forest (= Forrest Av), Lakeside, North, West, Parmly, Sanford Pl (= Ward Lane), Roosevelt/Centre (= Center Street), Black Point Rd, Avenue of Two Rivers; Parmly Property blank on west half. One part.

sheet-100-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 100, an additional sheet dated January 1922 at 120 ft to an inch, is the larger, lower-left portion of the sheet, set off from part 2 by a heavy line because the two parts are drawn about a kilometre apart on the ground. It shows the northeast corner of Rumson around Avenue of Two Rivers, which runs down the west edge. In the upper half the channels and loops of the North Shrewsbury River wind across marshy ground, mostly undrawn. In the lower half Black Point Road runs southeast from Avenue of Two Rivers towards Navesink Avenue at the lower right. South of it lie small blocks of narrow lots laid out between Avenue of Two Rivers, Maple Avenue and Cedar Avenue, crossed by Holly and Bay, with only a few dwellings built. The southwest corner holds a greenhouse range, a hollow tile foundry and the Hotel Monmouth near Ridge Road. Large undeveloped tracts, numbered 1, 2 and 4, fill the rest. The margins refer to sheet 99 to the west, 81 to the southwest and 82 to the southeast.
notes: Holly and Bay are today Holly Street and Bay Street.
The junction of Black Point Road and Navesink Avenue was not found where expected; that corner may have been realigned.
Hotel Monmouth stood near the corner of Avenue of Two Rivers and Ridge Road.

map, 120 ft to an inch. Two parts divided by a heavy line, about 1 km apart on the ground: part 1 lower left (Avenue of Two Rivers, Black Point Rd, Holly, Maple, Cedar, Bay, river loops); part 2 upper right (Lafayette, Washington, Bingham north of Hunt; Oceanic Rd to Forest St).

sheet-100-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 100, dated January 1922 at 120 ft to an inch, is the upper-right portion of the sheet, set off from part 1 by a heavy line. It shows the north end of the Oceanic district of Rumson along the North Shrewsbury River, north of sheet 80. Lafayette, Washington and Bingham Avenue run north from Hunt to the riverbank, where a pier with a dock and a bridge marked beside Washington reach into the river at the top left. Villa St. Ann and the Shrewsbury Inn stand between Lafayette and Washington. East of Bingham Avenue a large estate lot with a windmill and tank, garages and outbuildings runs down to Oceanic Road, with the Rumson Presbyterian Church at the corner of Bingham Avenue and Oceanic Road. Oceanic Road runs southeast across the lower part to Forest Street and a lane at the east edge, and long lots with a few dwellings and a coop run from the road to the river. The heavy line marks the edge of the part, with areas numbered 0 not mapped on this sheet. The margins refer to sheets 80 and 99.
notes: Oceanic Road is today East River Road; Forest Street is Forrest Avenue.
The bridge is drawn at the head of Washington; today's Oceanic Bridge lands at the foot of Bingham Avenue.

map, 120 ft to an inch. Two parts divided by a heavy line, about 1 km apart on the ground: part 1 lower left (Avenue of Two Rivers, Black Point Rd, Holly, Maple, Cedar, Bay, river loops); part 2 upper right (Lafayette, Washington, Bingham north of Hunt; Oceanic Rd to Forest St).
